newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' 91-day T-bill rate slips to 10.727 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' 91-day T-bill rate slips to 10.727 pct.

text.p: The Philippines' benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate slid to an average 10.727 percent at the weekly auction from 10.746 percent in the previous week, the Bureau of Treasury said on Monday.
Traders attributed the declining rates to excess liquidity in the system.
A total of 7.115 billion pesos worth of bids was received by the auction committee for the three-month bills, but it only accepted 1.0 billion pesos worth.
The average rate for the 182-day T-bills likewise went down to 11.004 percent from 11.106 percent, and the 364-day T-bill rate fell to 11.391 percent from 11.405 percent.
Banks tendered 5.87 billion pesos worth of bids for the six-month bills, and 4.97 billion pesos for the one-year bills.
The committee awarded only 1.5 billion pesos worth of bids for the six-month bills and 2.0 billion pesos for one-year bills.
